If pwd is not /Users/apple/velora, stop and say so. Do not rewrite history,
force-push, delete branches, or touch keys. Author is toibawani only. No
Co-authored-by trailers. No package.json or lockfile changes unless forced
(npm 10 if so, tell me).

GOAL: turn the real backlog into small, honest, separately pushed commits.
One commit is one finished, verified change. No empty commits, no
whitespace-only commits, no splitting one change into pieces to raise a
count, no touching a file just to touch it. If the backlog runs out before
30, stop and tell me the real number.

EACH COMMIT, EVERY TIME
1. git diff, read it, stage only the files for this one change
   (git add <paths>, never git add -A).
2. Run what the change touches: jest for the area, then lint, tsc and build
   before the push.
3. Commit with a plain message that says what was wrong or what is new, the
   way a person tells a teammate. No emoji, no repeated prefix, vary the
   wording. Examples:
     "Scrabble scored twice on a double click, settled the level first"
     "Dictionary letters with no entries are now dimmed, not clickable"
     "Remove the leftover .bak copy of the game audit"
4. git push origin main, then gh run list --limit 1 and paste the run URL
   and conclusion. Do not start the next commit until it is green. If it is
   red, diagnose the real cause before fixing.
5. git log -1 --format='%h %an <%ae> %s' to confirm the author.

BACKLOG, IN THIS ORDER (each bullet is one or more separate commits)
A. Housekeeping: finish any uncommitted half-done batch in the tree (fix
   counts without loosening tests); delete scripts/gameAudit.js.bak after
   checking it holds nothing current lacks; add .freebuff/ and other tool
   junk to .gitignore.
B. Lint debt in the 31 test files, one commit per rule group:
   no-container, no-node-access, jest/no-conditional-expect,
   render-result-naming, no-unnecessary-act, prefer-find-by, unused vars.
   After each group tests pass and three spot-checks still fail when the
   thing under test is broken. When lint:all is zero, add it to CI in its
   own commit.
C. Real GitHub Issues: gh issue create from docs/issues, one per issue,
   after checking each body is still true. Close each only with the commit
   that fixes it ("Fixes #n").
D. Hygiene: gh repo edit for description, website and topics; a commit-msg
   hook that rejects Co-authored-by trailers (prove it rejects one);
   commit hash references in docs/CASE-STUDY.md checked with git show.
E. Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md, SECURITY.md (what is protected, what is not, the
   limits of localStorage), WALKTHROUGH.md grounded in the real code. One
   commit per document.
F. Tests that prove checks can fail, one commit each: gameAudit fails when a
   game is broken, by-the-numbers changes when a data source changes,
   contrast checker fails on a bad token.
G. Content batches of 8 to 10 topics, one subject per batch, each topic with
   at least two sources whose URLs return 200, own words, concrete numbers,
   counters, resolver, README and by-the-numbers updated in the same commit
   and agreeing. Open every new topic in Chrome at 1440 and 375.
H. Dictionary batches for thin letters: definition, one clarifying example,
   source URL, honest verified flag.
I. Front-end fixes found by looking at screens at 1440, 375 and 320: one
   commit per screen or per bug (overflow, touch targets under 44px, missing
   focus ring, dead states).

REPORT every 5 commits: the hashes and messages (git log --oneline -5),
Actions conclusions, what you verified, mistakes you made, and what is left.
At the end run git shortlog -sne and gh api repos/toibawani/Velora/contributors
--jq '.[].login' and paste both. Never describe anything you did not run. make alot of commits with psuehs atleast 30

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  authorship:
    name: commit authorship
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # The range below reaches back past the pushed tip, so the whole
          # history has to be present.
          fetch-depth: 0
      # The local commit-msg hook in .githooks is the first line of defence and
      # it is configuration, not code: a fresh clone, a runner, or any tool that
      # passes --no-verify never sees it. This runs the same rule on the commits
      # that actually arrived, so a trailer or a foreign identity cannot be
      # pushed quietly even if the hook was bypassed.
      - name: every new commit is mine and carries no credit trailer
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            range="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}..${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
          else
            before="${{ github.event.before }}"
            if [ -z "$before" ] || [ "$before" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ] || ! git cat-file -e "$befor [… 5,880 characters omitted] yone but toibawani.
#
# Two things went wrong in this repository's history and neither was caught by
# reading the log: 41 commits carried a Co-Authored-By trailer naming an agent,
# and one commit was made as "apple <apple@apples-MacBook-Air.local>". The
# trailer is the easy one, because any tool that writes a commit message adds
# it; the identity is the quiet one, because a stray `git config` or a CI
# runner's default environment is enough to produce it.
#
# This hook runs at commit time, before the object exists, and exits non-zero
# so the commit never lands. scripts/commitAuthorship.js enforces the same
# rules in CI for commits that arrive by push or pull request.

msg_file="$1"
status=0

if [ -z "$msg_file" ] || [ ! -f "$msg_file" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: no message file given" >&2
	exit 1
fi

trailers=$(grep -in '^[[:space:]]*co-authored-by[[:space:]]*:' "$msg_file")
if [ -n "$trailers" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: refusing a Co-Authored-By trailer:" >&2
	echo "$trailers" | sed 's/^/  /' >&2
	echo "  Remove the line. Do not name an agent as an author of a commit." >&2
	status=1
fi

# `git var` resolves exactly the identity this commit will use, including
# GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL environment overrides, so this catches the
# case where the config is right and the environment is not.
author_ident=$(GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='@0 +0000' git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT 2>/dev/null)
author_name=${author_ident%% <*}
author_rest=${author_ident#*<}
author_email=${author_rest%%>*}

committer_ident=$(GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='@0 +0000' git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT 2>/dev/null)
committer_name=${committer_ident%% <*}
committer_rest=${committer_ident#*<}
committer_email=${committer_rest%%>*}

if [ "$author_name" != "toibawani" ] || [ "$author_email" != "toibawani14@gmail.com" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: author is '$author_name <$author_email>', not 'toibawani <toibawani14@gmail.com>'" >&2
	echo "  Fix with: git config user.name toibawani && git config user.email toibawani14@gmail.com" >&2
	status=1
fi

if [ "$committer_name" != "toibawani" ] || [ "$committer_email" != "toibawani14@gmail.com" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: committer is '$committer_name <$committer_email>', not 'toibawani <toibawani14@gmail.com>'" >&2
	status=1
fi

exit $status

# Issue 006: 375px checks on new lessons

## What is true right now

The layout audit (scripts/layoutCheck.js) checks horizontal overflow at 1440
and 375 pixels. It measures scrollWidth vs clientWidth on each screen. But
the check is only run on the main screens. When a new lesson is added, it is
not checked at 375px for overflow.

A new lesson might have content that fits at 1440px but overflows at 375px.
The audit does not catch it because the lesson is not in the SCREENS list.

## What I want

1. Add a new lesson to the layout check SCREENS list
2. Or add a generic check that walks all rendered screens
3. Document the 375px requirement for new content

## Why it matters

The app is used at 375px by someone. If the content overflows, they see a
horizontal scroll, which is a poor experience. This is a real user problem,
not a theoretical one.

## Notes

- The layout check uses real Chrome with Puppeteer
- The check measures scrollWidth - clientWidth at 375px
- The SCREENS list defines what screens are tested
- Adding a new lesson requires adding it to this list
===== docs/issues/007-npm-10-lockfile.md
# Issue 007: npm 10 lockfile generated with npx

## What is true right now

The lockfile is generated with npm 10, not npm 8. The CI uses npm ci which
exacts the lockfile. If someone runs npm ci on npm 8, it fails. The lockfile
is a contract between the package manager and the machine.

## What I want

1. Document the npm version required to generate the lockfile
2. Add a CI check that reports the npm version
3. Add a note to the README about the npm version requirement

## Why it matters

npm ci installs exactly what is in the lockfile. If the lockfile is from a
different npm version, npm ci fails. The lockfile is the source of truth for
the install. npm 10 changed internal defaults and the lockfile reflects that.

## Notes

- The package-lock.json is generated with npm 10
- The CI runs on Node 20 which ships with npm 10
- The devDependencies in package.json are pinned to specific versions

 * but it must resolve to 'unwritten' until someone writes it.

const hasLessonContent = (topic: { story?: unknown; sections?: unknown }): boolean =>

  && Array.isArray(topic.sections)
  && topic.sections.length > 0;

export type { DictionaryLetter, DictionarySubject, DictionarySubjectId, DictionaryTerm } from './types';
export { DICTIONARY_SUBJECTS };

/**
 * Everything the dictionary holds, in one list.
 *
 * This is the only module the app should import dictionary data from. The
 * per-subject files exist so adding a term means opening a short file, and the
 * grouping is a source-organisation detail that nothing outside here should
 * depend on.
 */
const ALL_TERMS: DictionaryTerm[] = [
  ...PHYSICS_TERMS,
  ...CHEMISTRY_TERMS,
  ...BIOLOGY_TERMS,
  ...PHILOSOPHY_TERMS,
  ...HISTORY_TERMS,
  ...POLITICAL_TERMS,
  ...MATH_TERMS,
  ...PSYCHOLOGY_TERMS,
  ...ECONOMICS_TERMS,
];

/**
 * A duplicate id would give two entries the same React key and the same anchor,
 * so the console would render both and jumping to either would land on the
 * first. The first one wins and the rest are dropped: a list that quietly
 * understates its own size is better than one that renders two cards for one
 * concept.
 */
function dedupeById(terms: DictionaryTerm[]): DictionaryTerm[] {
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const merged: DictionaryTerm[] = [];
  terms.forEach((term) => {
    if (term && term.id && !seen.has(term.id)) {
      seen.add(term.id);
      merged.push(term);
    }
  });
  return merged;
}

export const CURIOUS_TERMS: DictionaryTerm[] = dedupeById(ALL_TERMS);

{"kind":"tool","id":"eH2PZeQLg-Y","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"docs/ARCHITECTURE.md","instructions":"Add an architecture document grounded in the real modules and CI checks.","content":"# Architecture

What follows is the shape of the app as it exists in `src/`, not a plan. Every
file named here is one you can open; every number was read from the data files
or from `node scripts/by-the-numbers.js` on 26 October 2026.

## One paragraph

VELORA is a client-only React application built with Create React App. It has no
server, no accounts and no database. Content is TypeScript and JavaScript in
`src/data/`; state is localStorage, behind one registry; the build is a folder of
static files. A learner can open it on a school iPad, read, close the tab, and
come back without anything having been sent anywhere.

## Screens and routing

`src/App.js` holds the active screen in React state. There is no URL router: a
screen is a value, and `setScreen(id)` changes it. The screen bundles are loaded
with `React.lazy`, so the initial paint does not wait for the dictionary, the
games or the deep reads.

`src/navigation.js` is the registry of 13 screens. Each entry names the id, the
label in the bottom bar, the label in the drawer, a description and whether it is
primary. The navigation components render from this list, and so do the audits:
`scripts/layoutCheck.js` parses `SCREENS` rather than carrying its own copy, which
is why adding a screen gets it measured without editing the audit.

A lesson is not a screen. It opens inside Learn and is [… 4,281 characters omitted] s scroll
horizontally on purpose (subject rails, the A–Z bar), so the audit treats
`auto`/`scroll` ancestors as intentional and everything else as a defect.

## Checks

Jest covers the data, the utilities and the screens in jsdom. On 26 October 2026
that is 88 suites and 803 tests. It cannot see layout, which is why the rest are
real-Chrome scripts against `build/`:

| Script | What it proves |
|---|---|
| `layoutCheck.js` | every screen, and two lessons, has no element past the right edge at 1440 and 375, and logs no console error |
| `nameAudit.js` | screens use the names the navigation registry gives them |
| `gameAudit.js` | every game can be reached and played, and the page logs no error |
| `atlasAccessibilityAudit.js` | the Atlas search label and index are usable |
| `atlasTopicVerify.js` | every tapped topic resolves to a lesson, a deep read, or an honest "not written yet" |
| `atlasTapAudit.js` | every field and discipline has a live topic and every written topic's call to action opens content |
| `levelsVerify.js` | every black hole level renders real content |
| `checkContrast.js` | the composited design tokens meet WCAG AA |

`src/auditCoverage.test.js` checks the checks: every browser script is wired to
an npm script and to CI, resolves Chrome through `scripts/chrome.js`, can exit
non-zero on its own findings, and the layout audit still opens lessons.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has four jobs: commit authorship, tsc + Jest +
build + contrast + `lint:all`, the layout job, and the atlas job. A fifth
workflow deploys `build/` to GitHub Pages.

## Build and deploy

`npm run build` is CRA's build. The Pages workflow publishes the output. The
app is served from a subpath on Pages, and `scripts/auditServe.js` strips that
base path so the audits can serve `build/` at the root.

## Known limits

- No server means no sync, no recovery and no real account. This is a deliberate
  choice, documented in `docs/DECISIONS.md`, not an unfinished backend.
- localStorage is per browser and per origin. Private browsing can refuse writes;
  the storage module reports that rather than pretending a save worked.
- 456 of 572 Atlas topics have nothing to read yet and say so. The count is
  visible in the README, the roadmap and the app.
- The games are content checks with a score, not a game engine.

{"kind":"tool","id":"eIB6MDuzufE","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"docs/SECURITY.md","instructions":"Add a security document that states protections and limits honestly.","content":"# Security

This document states what VELORA protects, what it does not, and where the
limits are. It is about the app as it ships, not an aspiration.

## The short version

There is no server, no account and no session. The only data VELORA holds is
what a visitor types or reads on their own device, in that browser's
localStorage. Nothing is sent anywhere unless the visitor turns on the optional
analytics beacon, which is off by default.

That means the security model is mostly the browser's, and the honest summary is:
**anyone using the same browser profile can read and change everything VELORA
has stored.** The app is built for a shared school iPad, but it cannot defend
that iPad against the next person who picks it up.

## What is protected

- **No credentials are collected.** No password, email, phone number or account.
  The profile is a display name, 2–40 characters, kept under
  `velora_local_profile` and used only to greet the reader. It is not a login and
  is not checked against anything.
- **Nothing leaves the browser by default.** `src/utils/siteAnalytics.js` gates
  every beacon on `velora_analytics_optin`, which defaults to false. With it off,
  the module returns before touching the network. The privacy screen says so,
  and the code path matches the screen.
- **Rendered text is escaped by React.** Nothing in `src/` uses
  `dangerou [… 1,868 characters omitted] ts cover.
- **Client-side validation is not a control.** `validatePayload` and the
  injection pattern run in the page. They catch bad input and corrupt stored
  records; they do not defend against someone who can run JavaScript in the page.
- **The analytics opt-in is a promise, not a guarantee.** If the code is changed
  to send without checking the flag, nothing in the test suite would notice.
- **No encryption at rest.** Everything is plain JSON in localStorage. A person
  with access to the device's storage can read it.

## The limits of localStorage

- It is per origin and per browser profile. Clearing site data removes the
  profile, saved lessons, review schedule, questions and notes.
- It is usually capped around 5 MB per origin. When the quota is hit, writes fail
  and the app reports that instead of dropping data silently.
- Private browsing and some managed school profiles refuse storage entirely. The
  app still works for reading; it says nothing can be saved.
- It can be changed by any script on the same origin. There is no server copy to
  correct it against.

## Threat model, in plain terms

| Scenario | What happens |
|---|---|
| A classmate opens the app on the same iPad | They see the previous reader's name, progress and notes. The app cannot prevent this; clearing site data or using a separate profile does. |
| Someone edits localStorage | They can change their own progress. Nothing is shared, so nothing is defaced for anyone else. |
| A malicious script runs on the page | React escaping protects rendered text, but there is no CSP, and localStorage is readable. This is the gap to close first if the app ever accepts content from outside the repository. |
| The site is served over HTTP | GitHub Pages serves HTTPS. There is no mixed content: fonts are self-hosted and there are no third-party scripts. |
| Analytics is enabled | Page path, page title, topic opened, game id and a 7-day return count are sent to GoatCounter. No identifier, no cookies, no fingerprinting. It is off until the visitor turns it on. |

## Reporting

There is no security contact and no bug bounty. Open an issue in the repository
with the steps to reproduce, and do not include anyone's stored data. If the
report is about a real vulnerability and the repository is public, say so
without publishing an exploit first.
"}}

This follows the app the way a first-time visitor meets it, and names the file
that renders each step. If a screen is described wrongly here, the code is
right and this page is wrong; open the file and fix this page.

## 1. Splash

`src/screens/Splash.js`. The wordmark, one sentence about what this is, and two
buttons: **Start learning** and **Look around first**.

- Start learning goes to the local profile.
- Look around first goes to the landing page, where the inventory is visible
  before anything asks for a name.

There is no email field, no password field and no "Sign in with" button anywhere
in this flow, because there is nothing to sign in to.

## 2. What should we call you?

`src/screens/LocalProfile.js`, step 1. One field, labelled **Display name**, and
a note that the name stays on this device. It has to be at least two characters.
Nothing is checked against a server, because there is no server.

Step 2 asks **What are you here for?** with a grid of subjects and a goal. The
answers are saved under `velora_onboarding_preferences` and shape what the atlas
opens first. Skipping is possible; nothing is gated on the answers.

The tour (`src/components/OnboardingTour.js`) can point at the atlas, Learn and
the dictionary, then gets out of the way.

## 3. The atlas

`src/screens/UniverseHome.js`. This is the home screen.  [… 2,702 characters omitted] er material already in
the app, not a separate course.

The drawer holds the screens that do not fit in the bottom bar:

- **Next up** (`src/screens/NextUp.js`) — things the reader asked to come back to.
- **Roadmap** (`src/screens/Roadmap.js`) — what is built, half-built and not
  started, with the atlas/lesson gap stated.
- **Settings** — theme and the answers given at setup.
- **Question desk** (`src/screens/Community.js`) — the reader's own questions and
  notes against them. There is no forum and no other people; the old seeded
  explanations were removed rather than dressed up as a community.
- **Intellectual Dialogues** — scripted conversations with historical figures,
  written from their surviving work.
- **Privacy** and **Terms** — what leaves the browser (nothing, by default) and
  what the app promises.

## 7. Insights and Journey

`src/screens/Analytics.js` and `src/screens/Journey.js` read the event log in
localStorage. Insights shows time actually spent and what it went on; Journey is
a timeline of sessions on this device. Neither is a score, and neither is sent
anywhere. Clearing site data empties both, and the screens say so rather than
showing a friendly zero it cannot explain.

## 8. Coming back

The profile, the last lesson, saved reviews, tasks and notes all live in
localStorage under the registry in `src/utils/storage.js`. On a new browser there
is nothing to restore, and nothing is missing from a server, because there is no
server. That is the trade the app makes: no account, no sync, no recovery.

- `scripts/gameAudit.js` plays the games and fails on a console error.
- Jest covers the data and the screen logic in jsdom, including the resolver's

The rule for a new screen is in `src/navigation.js`: add it to `SCREENS` and the

/**
 * Where each option is drawn on screen.
 *
 * The options were rendered in the order they are written in the data, and the
 * data happens to put the right answer first on five of the fourteen questions
 * and second on most of the rest. Nothing shuffled them, so a player who never
 * read a word could score well by always taking A, and a player who did read
 * them learned "the long one is usually right" - the answer's position was
 * information about the deck rather than about the subject.
 *
 * Deterministic rather than random: the same question always lays out the same
 * way, so a re-render cannot move the options while a finger is on the way to
 * one, and a replay of a question the player just saw is not a new guess at
 * where the answer went. What it removes is the fixed link between a question
 * and the slot its answer sits in, which is the thing that was being learned.
 */
function optionOrder(questionIndex, count) {
  const stride = count > 2 ? count - 1 : 1;
  const offset = (questionIndex * 5 + 1) % count;
  const order = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) order.push((offset + i * stride) % count);
  const isIdentity = order.every((value, position) => value === position);
  return isIdentity ? order.slice().reverse() : order;
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"faoj-zOlo1A","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/utils/gameResults.js","instructions":"Add a module that records and reads per-game best results from versioned storage.","content":"/**
 * What the games have actually produced on this device.
 *
 * Six games each kept their round in component state, which meant the number a
 * player earned disappeared the moment they went back to the hub, and the hub
 * itself could say nothing about any game except its name. Someone deciding
 * what to play had no way to tell that they had never finished Concept
 * Scrabble, and someone who had just scored 1200 in Word Puzzle had no way to
 * see it beat last week's round.
 *
 * Two values per game, and neither invents a comparison the games do not
 * support:
 *
 *   best  - the highest score seen, kept alongside `max` because the games are
 *           not scored on the same scale. Concept Scrabble pays 500 a term and
 *           Concept Check pays 10 a question, so a bare "1600" would invite a
 *           comparison between rounds that were not measuring the same thing.
 *   plays - rounds finished. Started and abandoned does not count, because the
 *           games only report when they reach their own end screen.
 *
 * Nothing here is a measure of understanding and the hub does not present it as
 * one. It is a record of what happened, which is the only thing a score is.
 */
import { KEYS, readValue, writeValue } from './storage';

/** The shape stored under KEYS.GAME_RESULTS: game id to one record. */
export const EMPTY_RESULTS = {};

const isRecord = (value) =>
  value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value);

/**
 * Every game's record, with anything malformed left out.
 *
 * Storage is shared with older builds and with whatever a person typed into a
 * devtools console, so this reads defensively rather than trusting the shape:
 * a damaged entry is dropped, not thrown, because a hub that refuses to render
 * is worse than a hub that has forgotten one score.
 */
export function getGameResults() {
  const stored = readValue(KEYS.GAME_RESULTS, EMPTY_RESULTS);
  if (!isRecord(stored)) return { ...EMPTY_RESULTS };

  const results = {};
  Object.entries(stored).forEach(([gameId, record]) => {
    if (!isRecord(record)) return;
    const best = Number(record.best);
    const max = Number(record.max);
    const plays = Number(record.plays);
    results[gameId] = {
      best: Number.isFinite(best) ? best : 0,
      max: Number.isFinite(max) ? max : 0,
      plays: Number.isFinite(plays) && plays > 0 ? Math.floor(plays) : 0,
      at: typeof record.at === 'string' ? record.at : null,
    };
  });
  return results;
}

/** One game's record, or null if that game has never reached its own end screen. */
export function getGameResult(gameId) {
  return getGameResults()[gameId] || null;
}

/**
 * Records a finished round and returns the record as it now stands.
 *
 * `plays` always increments; `best` only when this round beat the stored one,
 * which is why it is kept next to the score it was earned on rather than
 * compared against a number of unknown scale. `id` is never guessed from a
 * name, so a renamed game keeps its history.
 */
export function recordGameResult(gameId, { score, max } = {}) {
  if (typeof gameId !== 'string' || !gameId) return null;

  const results = getGameResults();
  const previous = results[gameId] || { best: 0, max: 0, plays: 0, at: null };

  const numericScore = Number(score);
  const numericMax = Number(max);
  const score_ = Number.isFinite(numericScore) ? numericScore : 0;
  const maxValue = Number.isFinite(numericMax) ? numericMax : previous.max;

  const record = {
    best: Math.max(previous.best, score_),
    max: Math.max(previous.max, maxValue),
    plays: previous.plays + 1,
    at: new Date().toISOString(),
  };

  const next = { ...results, [gameId]: record };
  writeValue(KEYS.GAME_RESULTS, next);
  return record;
}

/** The game most recently finished, or null. The hub offers to reopen it. */
export function getLastPlayedGame() {
  const results = getGameResults();
  let latest = null;
  Object.entries(results).forEach(([gameId, record]) => {
    if (!record.at) return;
    if (!latest || record.at > latest.at) latest = { gameId, ...record };
  });
  return latest;
}

/**
 * "1200 of 1600" rather than "1200".
 *
 * The rounds are scored on different scales, so the fraction is what makes a
 * score mean anything at all on a grid where six of them sit side by side.
 */
export function formatResult(record) {
  if (!record) return '';
  return record.max > 0 ? `${record.best} of ${record.max}` : `${record.best}`;
}

export default getGameResults;

{"kind":"tool","id":"fap7mwM09DY","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/utils/gameResults.test.js","instructions":"Add tests covering the game results module.","content":"import {
  getGameResults,
  getGameResult,
  recordGameResult,
  getLastPlayedGame,
  formatResult,
} from './gameResults';
import { KEYS } from './storage';

beforeEach(() => {
  window.localStorage.clear();
});

test('a device that has never finished a round reports nothing, not zero', () => {
  expect(getGameResults()).toEqual({});
  expect(getGameResult('puzzle')).toBeNull();
  expect(getLastPlayedGame()).toBeNull();
});

test('a finished round is remembered with what it was scored out of', () => {
  recordGameResult('puzzle', { score: 1200, max: 1600 });
  expect(getGameResult('puzzle')).toMatchObject({ best: 1200, max: 1600, plays: 1 });
});

test('a worse round counts as a play without replacing the best', () => {
  recordGameResult('puzzle', { score: 1200, max: 1600 });
  recordGameResult('puzzle', { score: 400, max: 1600 });
  expect(getGameResult('puzzle')).toMatchObject({ best: 1200, plays: 2 });
});

test('a better round takes over', () => {
  recordGameResult('puzzle', { score: 400, max: 1600 });
  recordGameResult('puzzle', { score: 1500, max: 1600 });
  expect(getGameResult('puzzle')).toMatchObject({ best: 1500, plays: 2 });
});

test('games keep separate records, so one scale cannot flatter another', () => {
  recordGameResult('scrabble', { score: 500, max: 5000 });
  recordGameResult('quiz', { score: 140, max: 140 });
  expect(getGameResults().scrabble).toMatchObject({ best: 500, max: 5000 });
  expect(getGameResults().quiz).toMatchObject({ best: 140, max: 140 });
});

test('the most recently finished game is the one offered back', () => {
  recordGameResult('quiz', { score: 10, max: 140 });
  recordGameResult('chain', { score: 30, max: 30 });
  expect(getLastPlayedGame().gameId).toBe('chain');
});

test('a stored entry that is not a record is dropped rather than trusted', () => {
  window.localStorage.setItem(
    KEYS.GAME_RESULTS,
    JSON.stringify({ v: 1, data: { quiz: 'nonsense', chain: { best: 3, max: 4, plays: 1 } } })
  );
  const results = getGameResults();
  expect(results.quiz).toBeUndefined();
  expect(results.chain).toMatchObject({ best: 3, plays: 1 });
});

test('a score stored as text or a negative play count is not passed through', () => {
  window.localStorage.setItem(
    KEYS.GAME_RESULTS,
    JSON.stringify({ v: 1, data: { quiz: { best: '140', max: 140, plays: -2 } } })
  );
  expect(getGameResult('quiz')).toMatchObject({ best: 140, plays: 0 });
});

test('a game with no id is not recorded', () => {
  expect(recordGameResult('', { score: 1 })).toBeNull();
  expect(getGameResults()).toEqual({});
});

test('the fraction is what a score is shown as, because the scales differ', () => {
  expect(formatResult({ best: 1200, max: 1600 })).toBe('1200 of 1600');
  expect(formatResult({ best: 3, max: 0 })).toBe('3');
  expect(formatResult(null)).toBe('');
});
"}}

export function getLastPlayedGame() {
  const results = getGameResults();
  let latest = null;
  Object.entries(results).forEach(([gameId, record]) => {
    if (!record.at) return;
    if (!latest || record.at > latest.at) latest = { gameId, ...record };
  });
  return latest;
}

/**
 * The moment this round finished, never the same as the last one recorded.
 *
 * Two rounds can finish inside the same millisecond - a one-question replay, or
 * a pair of games closed seconds apart by a fast clicker - and a shared
 * timestamp makes "which was played last" depend on the order keys happen to
 * sit in a stored object. Bumping past the previous stamp costs nothing and
 * means the hub's offer to reopen a game cannot point at the wrong one.
 */
function nextStamp() {
  const previous = getLastPlayedGame();
  const now = Date.now();
  if (previous && Date.parse(previous.at) >= now) return new Date(Date.parse(previous.at) + 1).toISOString();
  return new Date(now).toISOString();
}","allowMultiple":false},{"oldString":"    at: new Date().toISOString(),","newString":"    at: nextStamp(),","allowMultiple":false}]}}

+/**
+ * What the games have actually produced on this device.
+ *
+ * Six games each kept their round in component state, which meant the number a
+ * player earned disappeared the moment they went back to the hub, and the hub
+ * itself could say nothing about any game except its name. Someone deciding
+ * what to play had no way to tell that they had never finished Concept
+ * Scrabble, and someone who had just scored 1200 in Word Puzzle had no way to
+ * see it beat last week's round.
+ *
+ * Two values per game, and neither invents a comparison the games do not
+ * support:
+ *
+ *   best  - the highest score seen, kept alongside `max` because the games are
+ *           not scored on the same scale. Concept Scrabble pays 500 a term and
+ *           Concept Check pays 10 a question, so a bare "1600" would invite a
+ *           comparison between rounds that were not measuring the same thing.
+ *   plays - rounds finished. Started and abandoned does not count, because the
+ *           games only report when they reach their own end screen.
+ *
+ * Nothing here is a measure of understanding and the hub does not present it as
+ * one. It is a record of what happened, which is the only thing a score is.
+ */
+import { KEYS, readValue, writeValue } from './storage';
+
+/** The shape stored under KEYS.GAME_RESULTS: game id to one record. */
+export const EMPTY_RESULTS = {};
+
+const isRecord = (value) =>
+  value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value);
+
+/**
+ * Every game's record, with anything malformed left out.
+ *
+ * Storage is shared with older builds and with whatever a person typed into a
+ * devtools console, so this reads defensively rather than trusting the shape:
+ * a damaged entry is dropped, not thrown, because a hub that refuses to render
+ * is worse than a hub that has forgotten one score.
+ */
+export function getGameResults() {
+  const stored = readValue(KEYS.GAME_RESULTS, EMPTY_RESULTS);
+  if (!isRecord(stored)) return { ...EMPTY_RESULTS };
+
+  const results = {};
+  Object.entries(stored).forEach(([gameId, record]) => {
+    if (!isRecord(record)) return;
+    const best = Number(record.best);
+    const max = Number(record.max);
+    const plays = Number(record.plays);
+    results[gameId] = {
+      best: Number.isFinite(best) ? best : 0,
+      max: Number.isFinite(max) ? max : 0,
+      plays: Number.isFinite(plays) && plays > 0 ? Math.floor(plays) : 0,
+      at: typeof record.at === 'string' ? record.at : null,
+    };
+  });
+  return results;
+}
+
+/** One game's record, or null if that game has never reached its own end screen. */
+export function getGameResult(gameId) {
+  return getGameResults()[gameId] || null;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Records a finished round and returns the record as it now stands.
+ *
+ * `plays` always increments; `best` only when this round beat the stored one,
+ * which is why it is kept next to the score it was earned on rather than
+ * compared against a number of unknown scale. `id` is never guessed from a
+ * name, so a renamed game keeps its history.
+ */
+export function recordGameResult(gameId, { score, max } = {}) {
+  if (typeof gameId !== 'string' || !gameId) return null;
+
+  const results = getGameResults();
+  const previous = results[gameId] || { best: 0, max: 0, plays: 0, at: null };
+
+  const numericScore = Number(score);
+  const numericMax = Number(max);
+  const rounded = Number.isFinite(numericScore) ? numericScore : 0;
+  const maxValue = Number.isFinite(numericMax) ? numericMax : previous.max;
+
+  const record = {
+    best: Math.max(previous.best, rounded),
+    max: Math.max(previous.max, maxValue),
+    plays: previous.plays + 1,
+    at: nextStamp(),
+  };
+
+  const next = { ...results, [gameId]: record };
+  writeValue(KEYS.GAME_RESULTS, next);
+  return record;
+}
+
+/** The game most recently finished, or null. The hub offers to reopen it. */
+export function getLastPlayedGame() {
+  const results = getGameResults();
+  let latest = null;
+  Object.entries(results).forEach(([gameId, record]) => {
+    if (!record.at) return;
+    if (!latest || record.at > latest.at) latest = { gameId, ...record };
+  });
+  return latest;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The moment this round finished, never the same as the last one recorded.
+ *
+ * Two rounds can finish inside the same millisecond - a one-question replay, or
+ * a pair of games closed seconds apart by a fast clicker - and a shared
+ * timestamp makes "which was played last" depend on the order keys happen to
+ * sit in a stored object. Bumping past the previous stamp costs nothing and
+ * means the hub's offer to reopen a game cannot point at the wrong one.
+ */
+function nextStamp() {
+  const previous = getLastPlayedGame();
+  const now = Date.now();
+  if (previous && Date.parse(previous.at) >= now) return new Date(Date.parse(previous.at) + 1).toISOString();
+  return new Date(now).toISOString();
+}
+
+/**
+ * "1200 of 1600" rather than "1200".
+ *
+ * The rounds are scored on different scales, so the fraction is what makes a
+ * score mean anything at all on a grid where six of them sit side by side.
+ */
+export function formatResult(record) {
+  if (!record) return '';
+  return record.max > 0 ? `${record.best} of ${record.max}` : `${record.best}`;
+}
+
+export default getGameResults;

+import {
+  getGameResults,
+  getGameResult,
+  recordGameResult,
+  getLastPlayedGame,
+  formatResult,
+} from './gameResults';
+import { KEYS } from './storage';
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  window.localStorage.clear();
+});
+
+test('a device that has never finished a round reports nothing, not zero', () => {
+  expect(getGameResults()).toEqual({});
+  expect(getGameResult('puzzle')).toBeNull();
+  expect(getLastPlayedGame()).toBeNull();
+});
+
+test('a finished round is remembered with what it was scored out of', () => {
+  recordGameResult('puzzle', { score: 1200, max: 1600 });
+  expect(getGameResult('puzzle')).toMatchObject({ best: 1200, max: 1600, plays: 1 });
+});
+
+test('a worse round counts as a play without replacing the best', () => {
+  recordGameResult('puzzle', { score: 1200, max: 1600 });
+  recordGameResult('puzzle', { score: 400, max: 1600 });
+  expect(getGameResult('puzzle')).toMatchObject({ best: 1200, plays: 2 });
+});
+
+test('a better round takes over', () => {
+  recordGameResult('puzzle', { score: 400, max: 1600 });
+  recordGameResult('puzzle', { score: 1500, max: 1600 });
+  expect(getGameResult('puzzle')).toMatchObject({ best: 1500, plays: 2 });
+});
+
+test('games keep separate records, so one scale cannot flatter another', () => {
+  recordGameResult('scrabble', { score: 500, max: 5000 });
+  recordGameResult('quiz', { score: 140, max: 140 });
+  expect(getGameResults().scrabble).toMatchObject({ best: 500, max: 5000 });
+  expect(getGameResults().quiz).toMatchObject({ best: 140, max: 140 });
+});
+
+test('the most recently finished game is the one offered back', () => {
+  recordGameResult('quiz', { score: 10, max: 140 });
+  recordGameResult('chain', { score: 30, max: 30 });
+  expect(getLastPlayedGame().gameId).toBe('chain');
+});
+
+test('a stored entry that is not a record is dropped rather than trusted', () => {
+  window.localStorage.setItem(
+    KEYS.GAME_RESULTS,
+    JSON.stringify({ v: 1, data: { quiz: 'nonsense', chain: { best: 3, max: 4, plays: 1 } } })
+  );
+  const results = getGameResults();
+  expect(results.quiz).toBeUndefined();
+  expect(results.chain).toMatchObject({ best: 3, plays: 1 });
+});
+
+test('a score stored as text or a negative play count is not passed through', () => {
+  window.localStorage.setItem(
+    KEYS.GAME_RESULTS,
+    JSON.stringify({ v: 1, data: { quiz: { best: '140', max: 140, plays: -2 } } })
+  );
+  expect(getGameResult('quiz')).toMatchObject({ best: 140, plays: 0 });
+});
+
+test('a game with no id is not recorded', () => {
+  expect(recordGameResult('', { score: 1 })).toBeNull();
+  expect(getGameResults()).toEqual({});
+});
+
+test('the fraction is what a score is shown as, because the scales differ', () => {
+  expect(formatResult({ best: 1200, max: 1600 })).toBe('1200 of 1600');
+  expect(formatResult({ best: 3, max: 0 })).toBe('3');
+  expect(formatResult(null)).toBe('');
+});

#!/bin/sh
# Refuse commits that credit anyone but toibawani.
#
# Two things went wrong in this repository's history and neither was caught by
# reading the log: 41 commits carried a Co-Authored-By trailer naming an agent,
# and one commit was made as "apple <apple@apples-MacBook-Air.local>". The
# trailer is the easy one, because any tool that writes a commit message adds
# it; the identity is the quiet one, because a stray `git config` or a CI
# runner's default environment is enough to produce it.
#
# This hook runs at commit time, before the object exists, and exits non-zero
# so the commit never lands. scripts/commitAuthorship.js enforces the same
# rules in CI for commits that arrive by push or pull request.

msg_file="$1"
status=0

if [ -z "$msg_file" ] || [ ! -f "$msg_file" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: no message file given" >&2
	exit 1
fi

trailers=$(grep -in '^[[:space:]]*co-authored-by[[:space:]]*:' "$msg_file")
if [ -n "$trailers" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: refusing a Co-Authored-By trailer:" >&2
	echo "$trailers" | sed 's/^/  /' >&2
	echo "  Remove the line. Do not name an agent as an author of a commit." >&2
	status=1
fi

# `git var` resolves exactly the identity this commit will use, including
# GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL environment overrides, so this catches the
# case where the config is right and the environment is not.
author_ident=$(GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='@0 +0000' git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT 2>/dev/null)
author_name=${author_ident%% <*}
author_rest=${author_ident#*<}
author_email=${author_rest%%>*}

committer_ident=$(GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='@0 +0000' git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT 2>/dev/null)
committer_name=${committer_ident%% <*}
committer_rest=${committer_ident#*<}
committer_email=${committer_rest%%>*}

if [ "$author_name" != "toibawani" ] || [ "$author_email" != "toibawani14@gmail.com" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: author is '$author_name <$author_email>', not 'toibawani <toibawani14@gmail.com>'" >&2
	echo "  Fix with: git config user.name toibawani && git config user.email toibawani14@gmail.com" >&2
	status=1
fi

if [ "$committer_name" != "toibawani" ] || [ "$committer_email" != "toibawani14@gmail.com" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: committer is '$committer_name <$committer_email>', not 'toibawani <toibawani14@gmail.com>'" >&2
	status=1
fi

exit $status

 * reviewPlanner
 *
 * The schedule of lessons someone asked to be reminded of, and when each one

 * Two things changed here, and both were about the schedule claiming less than

 * `retention` percentage that nothing measured. Neither is written any more.
 * What is stored is `reviews`: how many times the item has actually been
 * reviewed on this device. That is a count of an event, which is why it is
 * allowed to be stored.

const STORAGE_KEY = KEYS.REVIEWS;

export const removeReviewItem = (id) => {
  const nextItems = getReviewItems().filter((item) => item.id !== id);
  saveReviewItems(nextItems);
  return nextItems;

/**
 * Records that a review happened and moves the item one step along the ladder.
 *
 * The next date is measured from now, not from the date it was due: reviewing
 * three days late should not immediately make the item due again.
 */
export const completeReviewItem = (id, now = new Date()) => {
  const nextItems = getReviewItems()
    .map((item) => {
      if (item.id !== id) return item;
      const reviews = item.reviews + 1;
      return {
        ...item,
        reviews,
        lastReviewed: now.toISOString(),
        nextReview: new Date(now.getTime() + intervalForStep(reviews) * DAY).toISOString(),
      };
    })
    .sort(byNextReview);
  saveReviewItems(nextItems);
  return nextItems;
};

/**
 * Pushes an item back by a day without counting it as reviewed.
 *
 * "Not today" is a real answer, and without it the only way to silence a due
 * item was to press Review, which falsely told the schedule the lesson had been
 * recalled. Snoozing changes the date and leaves the count alone.
 */
export const snoozeReviewItem = (id, days = 1, now = new Date()) => {
  const shift = Number.isFinite(days) && days > 0 ? Math.floor(days) : 1;
  const nextItems = getReviewItems()
    .map((item) =>
      item.id === id
        ? { ...item, nextReview: new Date(now.getTime() + shift * DAY).toISOString() }
        : item,
    )
    .sort(byNextReview);
  saveReviewItems(nextItems);
  return nextItems;
};

/** "Step 2 of 5" for an item, used to show where it sits on the ladder. */
export const stepLabel = (item) => {
  const step = Math.min((item?.reviews || 0) + 1, REVIEW_LADDER.length);
  return `Step ${step} of ${REVIEW_LADDER.length}`;
};

import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { Calendar, BookOpen } from 'lucide-react';
import EmptyState from './EmptyState';
import { getReviewItems, reviewStatus, stepLabel } from '../utils/reviewPlanner';
import '../styles/SmartRevision.css';

/**
 * SmartRevision - the lessons this device saved, and when each comes due.
 *
 * It used to render three hard-coded rows ("Event Horizon Mechanics",
 * "Gravitational Singularity", "Inertial Frames") with next-review dates and
 * recall scores of 65, 45 and 92, above the line "Optimal recall intervals
 * calculated from your active retrieval scores". Nothing calculated any of it,
 * and every visitor saw the same three rows on their first visit. The rows are
 * gone; what is shown now is the review schedule the planner actually stored.
 *
 * The date wording comes from `reviewStatus`, the same function the planner
 * uses, so the two lists cannot describe the same item differently. The badge
 * shows the ladder step rather than the old `difficulty: 'new'` field, which
 * nothing ever updated and which is no longer written at all - it would have
 * rendered an empty chip on every row.
 */
SmartRevision.propTypes = { selectedSubject: PropTypes.string };

function SmartRevision({ selectedSubject }) {
  const [reviews] = useState(getReviewItems);
  const visible = selectedSubject
    ? reviews.filter((item) => item.subject === selectedSubject)
    : reviews;
  const dueCount = visible.filter((item) => reviewStatus(item).days <= 0).length;

  return (
    <div data-testid="smart-revision" className="smart-revision">
      <div className="revision-header">
        <h2 className="revision-title">Review schedule</h2>
        <p className="revision-desc">
          Lessons you saved, with the date each one comes due. The list lives in this browser. There
          is no recall score, because nothing here measures recall.
        </p>
      </div>

      {visible.length === 0 ? (
        <EmptyState
          icon={<BookOpen size={28} aria-hidden="true" />}
          title="Nothing saved for review"
          description="Open a lesson and choose Save for review. It will appear here the next time you look."
        />
      ) : (
        <div className="revision-list">
          <p className="revision-count" role="status">
            {dueCount === 0
              ? `${visible.length} saved, none due right now`
              : `${dueCount} of ${visible.length} due now`}
          </p>
          {visible.map((item) => {
            const status = reviewStatus(item);
            return (
              <div key={item.id} className={`revision-item ${status.days <= 0 ? 'is-due' : ''}`}>
                <div className="revision-info">
                  <h4 className="revision-topic">{item.topic}</h4>
                  <div className="revision-meta">
                    <span className="meta-badge">{stepLabel(item)}</span>
                    <span className="meta-time">
                      <Calendar size={13} strokeWidth={1.5} aria-hidden="true" />
                      <span>{status.label}</span>
                    </span>
                  </div>
                </div>
              </div>
            );
          })}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

export default SmartRevision;

  const trimmed = String(text == null ? '' : text).trim();
  if (trimmed.length < MIN_LENGTH || trimmed.length > MAX_LENGTH) {

          subject:

/**
 * VELORA utility module
 * resumePath
 *
 * "Pick up where you left off": remembers the last lesson opened so the atlas
 * can offer a one-tap resume. Stored as
 * { subject, topicId, topicTitle, openedAt } in localStorage; nothing leaves
 * the device.
 *
 * The key comes from utils/storage.js like every other key. This module used to
 * spell the raw key itself, which meant the registry's list of keys was missing
 * the one the resume card depends on: a rename in storage.js would have
 * silently orphaned every saved lesson.
 */

import { KEYS } from './storage';

const LAST_LESSON_KEY = KEYS.LAST_LESSON;

export const saveLastLesson = (subject, topicId, topicTitle) => {
  try {
    if (typeof window === 'undefined' || !window.localStorage) return false;
    const now = Date.now();
    window.localStorage.setItem(
      LAST_LESSON_KEY,
      JSON.stringify({ subject, topicId, topicTitle, openedAt: now }),
    );
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
};

export const getLastLesson = () => {
  try {
    if (typeof window === 'undefined' || !window.localStorage) return null;
    const raw = window.localStorage.getItem(LAST_LESSON_KEY);
    if (!raw) return null;
    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
    if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object') return null;
    if (!parsed.subject || !parsed.topicId) return null;
    return parsed;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
};

export const clearLastLesson = () => {
  try {
    if (typeof window === 'undefined' || !window.localStorage) return false;
    window.localStorage.removeItem(LAST_LESSON_KEY);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
};

const resumePath = { saveLastLesson, getLastLesson, clearLastLesson };

export default resumePath;

/**

 * Only the lesson that is actually open can be annotated: a late scroll event

export const saveLessonProgress = (subject, topicId, percent) => {

  test('starts with nothing to resume', () => {
    expect(getLastLesson()).toBeNull();
  });

  test('saves and reads back the last lesson', () => {
    expect(saveLastLesson('physics', 'black-holes', 'Black Holes')).toBe(true);
    const lesson = getLastLesson();
    expect(lesson).toMatchObject({
      subject: 'physics',
      topicId: 'black-holes',
      topicTitle: 'Black Holes',
    });
    expect(typeof lesson.openedAt).toBe('number');
  });

  test('goes through the versioned registry rather than a bare key', () => {
    saveLastLesson('physics', 'black-holes', 'Black Holes');
    const raw = JSON.parse(window.localStorage.getItem(KEYS.LAST_LESSON));
    expect(raw.v).toBe(1);
    expect(raw.data.topicId).toBe('black-holes');
  });

  test('overwrites the previo [… 1,661 characters omitted] pened lesson has no position to resume', () => {
    expect(getLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes')).toBeNull();
  });

  test('records a position for the lesson that is open', () => {
    expect(saveLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes', 42)).toBe(true);
    expect(getLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes')).toBe(42);
  });

  test('will not stamp a position onto a different lesson', () => {
    // A scroll event arriving after the reader has moved on belongs to the page
    // it came from, not to the one now open.
    expect(saveLessonProgress('philosophy', 'platos-cave', 80)).toBe(false);
    expect(getLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes')).toBeNull();
  });

  test('rounds and clamps a position rather than storing nonsense', () => {
    saveLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes', 41.6);
    expect(getLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes')).toBe(42);

    saveLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes', 120);
    expect(getLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes')).toBe(100);

    saveLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes', -20);
    expect(getLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes')).toBe(0);
  });

    expect(saveLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes', 'halfway')).toBe(false);
    expect(getLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes')).toBeNull();
  });

  test('a 0% position is a real position, not an absence', () => {
    saveLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes', 0);
    expect(getLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes')).toBe(0);
  });

  test('only offers to resume between a paragraph in and almost finished', () => {
    expect(shouldOfferResume(null)).toBe(false);
    expect(shouldOfferResume(0)).toBe(false);
    expect(shouldOfferResume(RESUME_MIN_PERCENT - 1)).toBe(false);
    expect(shouldOfferResume(RESUME_MIN_PERCENT)).toBe(true);
    expect(shouldOfferResume(50)).toBe(true);
    expect(shouldOfferResume(RESUME_COMPLETE_PERCENT - 1)).toBe(true);
    expect(shouldOfferResume(RESUME_COMPLETE_PERCENT)).toBe(false);
    expect(shouldOfferResume(100)).toBe(false);
  });

  test('the progress is scoped to the lesson it names', () => {
    saveLessonProgress('physics', 'black-holes', 60);
    expect(getLessonProgress('philosophy', 'platos-cave')).toBeNull();
    expect(getLessonProgress()).toBe(60);
  });
});

## Changes Made

### `src/index.css`
- **Focus states**: Changed from hardcoded `--accent-primary` to the design token `--ring`, and expanded to cover all interactive elements (buttons, inputs, textareas, links, `[role="button"]`, `.interactive`) with consistent `border-radius: var(--radius-sm)`
- **Elevated focus styling**: Added a new block that provides consistent focus rings across the entire app
- **Card hover**: Added global card hover effect with `box-shadow: var(--shadow-md)` and `!important` override

### `src/styles/UniverseHome.css`
- **Theme toggle**: Enhanced `.uh-icon-button` with explicit `display: inline-flex`, `align-items:center`, `justify-content:center`, and smooth hover transitions
- **Cards (.uh-card)**: 
  - Changed border from `var(--border-default)` to `var(--border-subtle)` for softer edges
  - Added `box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm)` and `transition` for elevation and smooth interactions
  - Fixed responsive styles to use proper dimensions (260px min-width, 420px flex-basis, 520px max-width) instead of stretching full width

### `src/styles/Games.css`
- **Game cards (.game-card-large)**: Added `box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm)`, `transition` for box-shadow and transform, and hover state with `box-shadow: var(--shadow-md)` + `transform: translateY(-2px)` for a subtle lift effect
- Removed duplicate/old `.game-card-large:hover` block that conflicted with the new one

### Commit
- Commit message: "frontend: polish UI with professional styling - enhanced focus states, card elevation, subtle micro-interactions"
- Pushed to `origin/main`

The app now has consistent focus rings using the design token system, cards with subtle elevation and hover interactions, and a generally more polished professional appearance rather than the AI-generated look that was previously forcing every button into pills and every card into 24px rounding.

  border-radius: var(--radius-2xl);
  background: var(--bg-elevated);
  color: var(--text-primary);

.vl-card[data-interactive='true'],
button.vl-card,

  cursor: pointer;

button.vl-card:hover,

@keyframes vl-settle {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: translateY(var(--enter-distance));
  }
  to {
    opacity: 1;
    transform: translateY(0);
  }
}

.vl-settle {
  animation: vl-settle var(--enter-duration) var(--enter-ease) both;
  animation-delay: calc(min(var(--i, 0), 6) * 55ms);

  50%  { transform: translate3d(0, -10px, 0) rotate(1.5deg); }
  to   { transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0) rotate(0deg); }

.vl-drift {

#!/bin/sh
# Refuse commits that credit anyone but toibawani.
#
# Two things went wrong in this repository's history and neither was caught by
# reading the log: 41 commits carried a Co-Authored-By trailer naming an agent,
# and one commit was made as "apple <apple@apples-MacBook-Air.local>". The
# trailer is the easy one, because any tool that writes a commit message adds
# it; the identity is the quiet one, because a stray `git config` or a CI
# runner's default environment is enough to produce it.
#
# This hook runs at commit time, before the object exists, and exits non-zero
# so the commit never lands. scripts/commitAuthorship.js enforces the same
# rules in CI for commits that arrive by push or pull request.

msg_file="$1"
status=0

if [ -z "$msg_file" ] || [ ! -f "$msg_file" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: no message file given" >&2
	exit 1
fi

trailers=$(grep -in '^[[:space:]]*co-authored-by[[:space:]]*:' "$msg_file")
if [ -n "$trailers" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: refusing a Co-Authored-By trailer:" >&2
	echo "$trailers" | sed 's/^/  /' >&2
	echo "  Remove the line. Do not name an agent as an author of a commit." >&2
	status=1
fi

# `git var` resolves exactly the identity this commit will use, including
# GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL environment overrides, so this catches the
# case where the config is right and the environment is not.
author_ident=$(GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='@0 +0000' git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT 2>/dev/null)
author_name=${author_ident%% <*}
author_rest=${author_ident#*<}
author_email=${author_rest%%>*}

committer_ident=$(GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='@0 +0000' git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT 2>/dev/null)
committer_name=${committer_ident%% <*}
committer_rest=${committer_ident#*<}
committer_email=${committer_rest%%>*}

if [ "$author_name" != "toibawani" ] || [ "$author_email" != "toibawani14@gmail.com" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: author is '$author_name <$author_email>', not 'toibawani <toibawani14@gmail.com>'" >&2
	echo "  Fix with: git config user.name toibawani && git config user.email toibawani14@gmail.com" >&2
	status=1
fi

if [ "$committer_name" != "toibawani" ] || [ "$committer_email" != "toibawani14@gmail.com" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: committer is '$committer_name <$committer_email>', not 'toibawani <toibawani14@gmail.com>'" >&2
	status=1
fi

exit $status

/**
 * VELORA utility module
 * localProfile
 */
/**
 * The local profile.
 *
 * This app has no backend. It cannot verify an email, cannot store a password
 * safely, and cannot tell one person from another. The version it used to ship
 * asked for a phone number and a username it never read, then offered a "Log
 * out" for a session that had never existed. That is a trust problem, not a
 * polish item, so the identity model is now honest about what it is: a chosen
 * display name, held on this device, used only to greet you.
 *
 * Stored shape: { name: string, createdAt: string }
 */

import { KEYS, FAILURE, readValue, writeValue, removeValue } from './storage';

const STORAGE_KEY = KEYS.LOCAL_PROFILE;

const MAX_NAME_LENGTH = 40;

export const normalizeName = (value) =>
  String(value || '')
    .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
    .trim()
    .slice(0, MAX_NAME_LENGTH);

export const isValidName = (value) => normalizeName(value).length >= 2;

export const getProfile = () => {
  const parsed = readValue(STORAGE_KEY, null);
  if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object') return null;
  const name = normalizeName(parsed.name);
  if (!isValidName(name)) return null;
  return { name, createdAt: typeof parsed.createdAt === 'string' ? parsed.createdAt : null };
};

/*
 * A run of right answers, shown in the header only once it is worth noticing.
 * It sits beside the score rather than replacing it, because the score is the
 * number that gets recorded and the run is the number that describes how the
 * round felt. Accent-bordered and quiet: it must not compete with the question
 * underneath it, which is the thing being read.
 */
.quiz-streak {
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.02em;
  color: var(--text-secondary);
  background: var(--bg-secondary);

  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  padding: 2px var(--space-2);
  white-space: nowrap;
  animation: quiz-streak-in 0.18s var(--ease-standard);
}

@keyframes quiz-streak-in {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: translateX(-4px);
  }
  to {
    opacity: 1;
    transform: translateX(0);
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .quiz-streak {
    animation: none;
  }
}

.quiz-streak-summary {
  margin: var(--space-2) 0 0;
  font-size: 0.9375rem;
  color: var(--text-secondary);
}","allowMultiple":false}]}}

**What actually improved (games + content)**

Concept Check ([QuantumQuiz.js](src/games/QuantumQuiz.js)) gained 12 questions across economics, psychology, history, mathematics and politics — the five fields the app teaches but never quizzed — each grounded in a term already in [the dictionary](src/data/dictionary/index.ts).
